# Browser-driven verification (authenticated)

For any UI verification that needs a signed-in session (past the auth wall), mint a session cookie from the DB and drive the **paired Owletto extension** through the Lobu connector-operations bridge (`lobu call manage_operations`, or the SDK `operations` namespace). This runs in the user's real logged-in Chrome — no separate headless browser, no CDP, no extra browser tooling to install.

## Scope

The forged session cookie authenticates the **web admin REST mounted at `/`** (`/api/auth/*`, `/api/<orgSlug>/...`, the SPA — anything `lobu apply` and the web app talk to). It does **NOT** authenticate the **public Agent API at `/lobu`** (`/lobu/api/v1/agents/*`, `/lobu/api/v1/agents/<id>/sessions`) — that path expects a JWT bearer from the OAuth device flow (`lobu login`) or a PAT. If `/lobu/api/v1/agents` returns `401` despite a valid cookie, switch to `lobu chat` / `lobu token`.

## Pick a target

Local dev backend (with prod DB attached over Tailscale): `https://<your-tailscale-host>.ts.net:8443`. Prod: `https://app.lobu.ai`.

## Grab the secret + session token

```bash
# Local dev backend uses .env's BETTER_AUTH_SECRET
SECRET=$(grep '^BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=' .env | cut -d= -f2-)

# Prod uses the secret on the K8s pod
SECRET=$(kubectl exec -n summaries-prod \
  $(kubectl get pod -n summaries-prod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=lobu-app -o name | head -1 | sed 's|pod/||') \
  -- printenv BETTER_AUTH_SECRET)
```

Session token from the DB. With no local `DATABASE_URL` set, exec psql inside the prod DB pod (the prod DB serves both targets):

```bash
DBURL=$(kubectl exec -n summaries-prod <lobu-app-pod> -- printenv DATABASE_URL)
PGPASS=$(printf '%s' "$DBURL" | sed -E 's#.*://[^:]+:([^@]+)@.*#\1#')
TOKEN=$(kubectl exec -n summaries-prod lobu-ai-prod-db-1 -- \
  env PGPASSWORD="REDACTED" psql -h lobu-ai-prod-db-pooler -U summaries -d owletto -tAc \
  "SELECT token FROM session WHERE \"userId\" = '<user_id>' AND \"expiresAt\" > NOW() ORDER BY \"updatedAt\" DESC LIMIT 1")
```

## Sign the cookie

better-auth uses HMAC-SHA256, base64, then URL-encode — base64**url** does *not* validate.

```bash
SIGNED=$(SECRET="$SECRET" TOKEN="$TOKEN" node -e '
  const {createHmac}=require("node:crypto");
  const sig=createHmac("sha256",process.env.SECRET).update(process.env.TOKEN).digest("base64");
  console.log(encodeURIComponent(`${process.env.TOKEN}.${sig}`));
')
```

Cookie name is `__Secure-better-auth.session_token` whenever the baseURL is `https://` (prod and Tailscale dev qualify; only plain-http localhost uses the unprefixed `better-auth.session_token`).

## Find the Chrome connection

Browser actions dispatch to a paired Chrome extension connection (usually org `buremba`):

```bash
lobu call manage_connections --org buremba --arg action=list --raw
```

Pick the `chrome` connector with `status: active` on the machine whose browser you want to drive. `operations.listAvailable({ connection_id })` reports per-target `readiness` and `execution_targets` — use it to check the device is actually online before a long verification.

**Diagnosis — infinite navigation loop on the Activity page:**
1. When you scroll down, page 2 loads → the cursor sync effect writes the scroll position to the URL (`?sort_by=date&at=…` — exactly what appears in your screenshot's URL).

The cursor effect depends on `updateFilters` and has **no guard to check "is it the same cursor?"** → it fires again, writes the identical cursor → the router still runs `load()` for a replace-navigation to the same URL → new `location` → effect fires again → … infinite render/navigate loop → "Page Unresponsive".

## What the bug is (from your screenshot, via OCR)
`/buremba/activity?sort_by=date&at=2026-08-07T01:34:11.454Z,4849396` triggers Chrome's **"Page Unresponsive"** after you scroll down a little (which loads page 2 of the infinite feed).

## My leading root-cause hypothesis (well-supported, not proven)
The URL cursor-sync effect in `packages/owletto/src/components/entity-tabs/events-tab/index.tsx` (~line 686):

```ts
useEffect(() => {
  if (!useDateFeed || !lastLoadedItem || infiniteData?.pages.length === 1) return;
  updateUrlFilters({ beforeOccurredAt: lastLoadedItem.occurred_at, beforeId: lastLoadedItem.id });
}, [lastLoadedItem?.id, useDateFeed, updateUrlFilters, infiniteData?.pages.length, lastLoadedItem]);
```

Once page 2 lands it writes the scroll cursor into the URL. The loop I believe follows:
1. That navigate mints a fresh `location` (TanStack Router re-runs `load()` even on a same-URL replace — verified in `router.js`: `if (isSameUrl && isSameState()) this.load()`).
2. `useTabFilters.updateFilters` is a `useCallback` depending on the whole `location`, so it gets a new identity.
3. The effect depends on `updateUrlFilters`, re-fires, and writes the **same** cursor again → fresh location → forever. It's a navigate→render→effect storm that saturates the main thread. Note the sibling search-sync effect has an equality guard; **this one doesn't.**

Evidence it's the right area: page-1-only render settles fine in jsdom; something hangs right after the second page's cursor write; your URL already contains the `at=` cursor.

- Traced the router internals (`commitLocation`, `load`, location store `Object.is` compare).
- Built a jsdom repro with a controllable IntersectionObserver + MSW two-page fixture.
- Added navigate/history/fetch tripwires and event subscribers to catch the loop.

## Where I got stuck
The jsdom harness is itself unstable: `router.subscribe(...)` before first render wedges the router's initial load, and my instrumentation interacts with the hang, so I never captured a clean stack trace. My last runs hang between page-1-render and a plain `setTimeout`, which tells me the harness is polluting the signal. I could not get a clean red→green.

Add an idempotency guard so the effect never re-writes an identical cursor:

```ts
const next = { beforeOccurredAt: lastLoadedItem.occurred_at, beforeId: lastLoadedItem.id };
if (filters.beforeOccurredAt === next.beforeOccurredAt && filters.beforeId === next.beforeId) return;
updateUrlFilters(next);
```

**Done — shipped and verified on prod.** That screenshot's bug no longer exists.

## What it was
On `/$owner/activity`, loading the second infinite-scroll page wrote the scroll cursor into the URL (`?at=<ts>,<id>`). That navigation minted a fresh router `location` → `updateUrlFilters` got a fresh identity → the cursor-sync effect re-fired and rewrote the **same** cursor → another `load()` cycle → endless `navigate → render → effect` loop → main thread saturated → Chrome's "Page Unresponsive."

## The fix
A 7-line equality guard in `EventsTab` — never rewrite a cursor that already matches the URL (the sibling search-sync effect already had this guard). Plus a regression test.

| Red (real headless Chromium, prod data) | Tab freezes ~2s after page 2 loads; vitest worker hangs `exit 124` |
| Green (same browser, fixed code) | Page 2 loads, `?at=…` written **once**, scroll-up responsive |
